summary: Regression pass focused on the Phase 1 TEXT->TIMESTAMPTZ migration (52 columns / 22 tables). Ran the existing 33-test suite (tests/test_iter107_timestamptz_regression.py), then a shape/role-corrected follow-up suite (test_iter107b_ts_followup.py) and a bad-date-input fuzz suite (test_iter107c_bad_date_inputs.py). Frontend: attendee UI login (no MFA) -> dashboard/meetings list, and admin (cookie-injected) -> dashboard, New Meeting create, Organisation, Schedules, Team Themes, Settings. Result: exactly ONE real regression of the same class as the rate_limit.py bug — PATCH /api/review/{id}/speaker-text 500s because an empty string is written to the now-TIMESTAMPTZ transcripts.speaker_text_backup_at. Everything else (auth+MFA, lockout, rapid meeting creates through the fixed rate limiter, meetings list ordering/date filters, review edits/comments/audit-trail/signoff/reopen, org settings/teams/invitations, schedules, super-admin org+invite lifecycle, dashboard/admin reads) passed. All 6 remaining failures in the pre-existing iter107 suite were test-script assumptions (response shape, reopen role, email lower-casing), reproved green in 107b.

critical.issue: 500 on EVERY call. routers/review.py:1075 `values.append(existing_t.get("speaker_text_edited_at") or "")` passes '' into transcripts.speaker_text_backup_at, which is now TIMESTAMPTZ -> asyncpg.exceptions.InvalidDatetimeFormatError: invalid input syntax for type timestamp with time zone: "" (traceback at routers/review.py line 1083, repeated in /var/log/supervisor/backend.err.log lines 15924/16599/16995/17352). Breaks all speaker-label editing / rename / Flip-From-Here / split-turn saves. Fix: `or None` (and equally consider the sibling `speaker_text_backup_by` which is fine as text).

minor.issue: meetings.date is still TEXT and accepts arbitrary garbage: date='' , 'not-a-date', '2026-13-45' all return 201 and persist verbatim (pre-existing validation gap, not caused by the migration, but it will block any future date->DATE conversion).
Malformed/empty date_from/date_to are silently ignored (200 with unfiltered data) instead of 422. No 500s, so migration-safe, but silent filter drop is a correctness smell.

critical_code_review_comments: database.py's text-format timestamptz codec normalises Postgres output back to ISO ('YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS+00:00'), so all existing string comparisons (e.g. routers/auth.py:370/428 mfa_code_expires_at < now().isoformat()) still behave — verified working via MFA login + expired-code tests. Caveat: ISO string comparison is only lexicographically safe because the codec always emits UTC offsets; if a column ever returns a non-UTC offset the string compare will silently mis-order. Prefer comparing datetimes.

The `X or ""` idiom is the exact footgun that caused both the rate_limit.py and review.py 500s. A repo-wide grep now shows only review.py:1075 remaining for timestamp columns; consider a lint rule / helper (_ts_or_none) to prevent regressions.

rca_of_the_issue: Root cause: routers/review.py update_speaker_text builds a dynamic UPDATE and, when a prior transcript exists, backs up the previous edit metadata with `existing_t.get('speaker_text_edited_at') or ''`. Before Phase 1 that column was TEXT so '' was accepted; it is now TIMESTAMPTZ, so Postgres raises InvalidDatetimeFormatError and FastAPI returns 500. Reproduction: seed/pick any meeting whose transcript has speaker_text but a NULL speaker_text_edited_at, then PATCH /api/review/{id}/speaker-text -> 500 (test_iter107b_ts_followup.py::test_speaker_text_edit_no_500). Because the first edit never persists speaker_text_edited_at, the second edit fails identically — the endpoint is permanently broken, not just on first use. Mitigation: pass None instead of ''.
